3. When reproducing bugs guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen reproducing bugs approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Check that reproducing bugs terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Before starting reproducing bugs work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. When reproducing bugs decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Keep reproducing bugs outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. Prefer explicit, readable reproducing bugs solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

- Do not silently drop reproducing bugs edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
